account:
Today I attended market business, reviewed the treasury, and visited my neighbour for tea before returning to office hours. The treasury contains 128 emeralds, but the town accounts ledger and receipts have not been located. The secretary checked the four great hall tables: three were empty and one held bread. I do not know who normally prepares the accounts or whether their absence means anything beyond poor recordkeeping. I asked the secretary to inquire with the builder and innkeeper.

There is some unusual, unverified riverside gossip. My neighbour heard from Townsfolk 02 outside the bakery about a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' and also heard about bakery lights, although the baker reportedly knew of no celebration. My neighbour saw no change personally, and I have not verified any of this. I cannot yet tell whether these reports refer to actual work, a gathering, or simply muddled gossip.

The definite work I have heard about is in the great hall: the innkeeper says eight lanterns have been installed to light the tables. The builder's lighting inspection is scheduled for tomorrow at 18:00, and I have confirmed attendance. The secretary recorded it in an addendum, and both appointment books are secured in my appointments chest. The innkeeper repeatedly sought confirmation before explaining the work, but I have no evidence of a hidden purpose or connection to the bakery rumours. The secretary reports no new letters or urgent business. My next scheduled obligation is to be home at 19:00.
